analysis.title: Strong Earnings Growth & Attractive Seasonality May Favor Equity Overweight
key_insights: Sterling Capital favors an equity overweight in both large and small caps, arguing earnings resilience, seasonality and reasonable valuations let US equities look through Fed hike risk, the US-Iran conflict, elevated inflation and midterm elections into 2027.
Consensus EPS growth for 2026-2028 averages 21% a year for the S&P 500 and 19% a year for the S&P 600 small caps (FactSet, as of 09.18.2026).

Earnings growth has outpaced price in 2026, so the forward P/E has contracted and the S&P 500 is less expensive than at the start of the year. Sterling argues equities may be undervalued relative to earnings growth.

Sterling gives three reasons for the 2026 P/E compression: earnings grew faster than prices, rising yields raise the discount rate on future cash flows, and some investors think earnings are temporarily elevated.

Seasonality: October has historically been the best month of a midterm year (S&P 500 average +3%), and Q4 of a midterm year the best quarter. The third year of a presidential cycle has averaged +14.5% for the S&P 500, which Sterling applies to 2027.

Sterling attributes the midterm-year strength to the shift toward gridlock in Washington, which it calls a Goldilocks scenario because it tends to reduce policy risk. Futures markets are potentially expecting gridlock in 2026.

The report's text says hyperscalers (Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle) may invest $805B in AI infrastructure in 2026 and $1.1T in 2027, which Sterling treats as the key driver of large-cap earnings growth.
Semiconductors and power suppliers are named as sub-industries well positioned to meet hyperscaler shortages, with estimated 2026-2028 EPS growth of 55% and 18% a year per chart 4.
Versus 1999, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 trade at lower P/E ratios but show higher FCF/share and ROE in 2026E, which Sterling reads as higher quality and a cushion for investors.
Meta's AI assistant 'Muse' reached 5M downloads in under 2 weeks. Sterling notes about 7B smartphones exist, so AI agents have penetrated under 1% of that addressable market.

tension_points.bull_case: Earnings growth of 21% a year (S&P 500) and 19% a year (S&P 600) through 2028, P/E compression, midterm-year Q4 seasonality and gridlock lower policy risk.
tension_points.bear_case: A Fed rate hike in September, the US-Iran conflict, elevated inflation and midterm elections, plus rising yields that cut the multiple investors pay and a view that earnings are temporarily elevated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The report does not name a specific level or event. It frames earnings growth failing to hold through 2028 as the implied break.

theme_stances.evidence: October may be the best performing month of a midterm year
